sources.title: P4 Advanced Financial Management September/December 2016 - Official Answers
sources.use: Project duration and a worked selling-price sensitivity margin.
sources.finding: Duration is calculated as the PV-weighted average time. Selling-price headroom is NPV divided by the discounted, post-tax revenue cash flows affected.
sources.formula: Duration = Σ(t × PV_t) / ΣPV_t; selling-price sensitivity = NPV / PV of affected post-tax revenue cash flows.

sources.title: AFM September/December 2019 - Official Sample Answers
sources.use: Second, very explicit AFM project-duration calculation.
sources.finding: The answer totals PV × time and divides by total positive PVs, producing 3.04 years.
sources.formula: Project duration = total (PV × time) / total PV.

sources.title: F9 June 2016 Examiner’s Report
sources.use: Black-and-white statement of the general sensitivity formula.
sources.finding: The denominator must be the present value of the project variable affected, after relevant tax effects.
sources.formula: Sensitivity % = 100 × NPV / PV of project variable.

sources.title: FM September/December 2023 Examiner’s Report
sources.use: Current ACCA convention for variable sensitivity and discount-rate sensitivity.
sources.finding: For the discount rate, IRR minus the original rate is the absolute headroom in percentage points. ACCA says percentage sensitivity divides that change by the original rate.
sources.formula: Variable sensitivity % = NPV / PV of affected post-tax variable × 100. Discount-rate sensitivity % = (IRR − original discount rate) / original discount rate × 100.

sources.title: AFM March/June 2019 - Official Sample Answers
sources.finding: The answer identifies an 11% project-specific risk-adjusted cost of capital based on a proxy company asset beta, then discounts the project cash flows at 11%.
sources.formula: Use the project-specific RADR as the discount rate applied to the project’s relevant cash flows.

sources.title: FM March/June 2018 - Official Sample Answers
sources.use: Joint-probability ENPV table and ACCA explanation of RADR derivation.
sources.finding: The official answer constructs joint probabilities and ENPV, and explains that a proxy beta can be ungeared and regeared to obtain a project-specific discount rate.
sources.formula: ENPV = Σ(probability × outcome NPV); RADR may be derived through CAPM using a proxy beta ungeared and regeared.

sources.title: F9 June 2015 - Official Answers
sources.finding: The answer calculates an expected input using probabilities, carries it through the project cash-flow table, and labels the result ENPV.
sources.formula: Expected input = Σ(probability × outcome); ENPV is the NPV based on probability-weighted expected inputs/outcomes.

sources.title: AFM September 2018 - Official Answers (Airone / Washi Co)
sources.use: Calculator #11 (fxhedge.ts) FIX ROUND 2, 2026-07-23 - per-unit currency option premium formula, cited by the GPT adjudication round and independently re-verified here by direct fetch.
sources.finding: The official answer computes the option premium as a flat per-unit rate multiplied by the number of contracts and contract size, with NO time proration applied - confirming the FIX ROUND 1 K3 correction (an earlier engine version wrongly prorated by months/12, an unsourced import from an interest-rate-options formula).
sources.formula: Premium payable = premium per unit × contract size × number of contracts (worked: JPY 3.8 × 125,000 × 640 = JPY 304m).

sources.title: AFM March/June 2021 Examiner's Report (currency futures/options hedge question)
sources.use: Calculator #11 (fxhedge.ts) FIX ROUND 2, 2026-07-23 - full worked lock-in-rate calculation, cited by the GPT adjudication round ("MJ21") and independently re-verified here by direct fetch. Algebraically checked against the engine's own formula and found to be an EXACT match under a sign-convention transposition (see finding).
sources.finding: The report's own convention defines basis = opening futures price − spot rate (the OPPOSITE sign to this engine's basis0 = spot0 − futures0), and its lock-in formula is 'opening futures price − basis remaining'. Substituting the sign-flip shows this is algebraically IDENTICAL to this engine's lock_in_rate = futures0 + unexpired_basis - both routes compute exactly 0.2374 US$/MR1 on the worked figures. Also confirms premium-currency conversion (not proration) is the graded error class the examiner flags, matching GATE 18's scope.
sources.formula: Worked: current basis = 0.2378 − 0.2358 = 0.0020; basis remaining = 0.0020 × 1/5 = 0.0004; lock-in rate = 0.2378 − 0.0004 = 0.2374 US$/MR1.

technical_articles.title: How to answer a foreign exchange risk management question (ACCA P4/AFM technical article)
technical_articles.note: Live HTML page, not a stable PDF - no byte-guard applies; verified by direct WebFetch 2026-07-23.
technical_articles.use: Calculator #11 (fxhedge.ts) FIX ROUND 2 - (a) confirms a RECEIPT is hedged by SELLING futures (the direction/instrumentSide convention), (b) a second per-unit premium example (quoted in cents, not the notional's own major unit), (c) a second, independently-worded lock-in-rate example.
technical_articles.finding: Nutourne Co (USA-based) receives CHF and hedges by SELLING CHF futures — confirms the receipt-sells / payment-buys direction convention. Separately shows a premium quoted as 0.86 US cents per CHF unit (a currency-denomination nuance: the premium's quote currency need not match the notional's major-unit convention). A second lock-in-rate worked example (1.0369 − 0.0011 = 1.0358) is ALGEBRAICALLY the same formula as T1, confirming it is not a one-off phrasing.
technical_articles.formula: Verbatim: "Sell CHF futures now to hedge against sale of CHF when money received from Swiss customer."; premium: "Multiply number of contracts × size of one contract × 0.0086, as premium is quoted in US cents (not US dollars) per CHF."
